# Spec: WF-10 — Search businesses and create advertisers without duplicates

Status: Draft
Ticket: WF-10
Change kind: Modify
Supersedes: N/A
Approved by: —
Approved at: —

## Objective
Users search businesses through the Google Places API and create an advertiser from a result. An advertiser is a duplicate when any of its identity signals matches another advertiser: Google Place ID, normalized root domain, normalized name+ZIP, or normalized phone. Concurrent submissions that match on any signal MUST produce at most one advertiser. Place enrichment after creation MUST either retry or end in a visible failure state; it never stays pending forever.

Out of scope: design artifacts (the intake requires none), and changes to the companion service (DEC-001).

Source: supplied completed intake WF-10; user decisions in the /spec request of 2026-11-24.

## Change Impact
- Added behavior: multi-result business search through Google Places, called directly (REQ-001, REQ-002). Database-enforced identity uniqueness across all four signals (REQ-003–REQ-006). Bounded enrichment that always ends in a terminal state (REQ-007, REQ-008).
- Modified behavior: the existing application-level duplicate checks, which race under concurrency (intake recon), stop being the guarantee. The database constraint becomes the guarantee (REQ-005). The checks MAY remain as early user feedback.
- Removed behavior: this feature no longer uses the companion service. The companion service supports single-place lookup only, and DEC-001 replaces it here. Its other consumers are Not surveyed and are left unchanged.
- Explicitly preserved behavior: whoever may create advertisers today is the only one who may search and create through this flow (REQ-009). Existing advertiser data is not deleted or merged without an owner decision (OPEN QUESTION Q3).
- Compatibility/migration constraints: existing rows may already violate the new uniqueness rules, so the constraint cannot be added until they are resolved (Q3). Root domain lives on a separate website table (intake recon).

## Requirements

### Requirement: REQ-001 — Business search via Google Places
Source: intake WF-10 "search businesses"; DEC-001

When a user submits a business search query, the system MUST call the Google Places API directly, without the companion service, and MUST show every returned candidate with its name, address and Place ID.

#### Scenario: Query returns several businesses
- GIVEN Google Places returns 3 candidates for "acme plumbing 94107"
- WHEN the user submits that query
- THEN the system shows all 3 candidates, each with name, address and Place ID

#### Scenario: Query returns no businesses
- GIVEN Google Places returns zero candidates
- WHEN the user submits the query
- THEN the system shows an empty result state and creates no advertiser

### Requirement: REQ-002 — Search failure is visible and safe
Source: intake WF-10; DEC-004; spec-quality-gates §1 (timeout, partial failure, privacy)

If a Google Places request errors, times out after 10 s (DEC-004), or is refused for quota, then the system MUST show a search error state, MUST NOT create or change any advertiser, and MUST log the failure without the API key.

#### Scenario: Places times out
- GIVEN Google Places does not respond within 10 s
- WHEN the user submits a query
- THEN the user sees a search error, no advertiser row changes, and a log entry records the timeout without the API key

#### Scenario: API key stays server-side
- GIVEN any search request
- WHEN the browser receives the response
- THEN the response and the page contain no Google API key

### Requirement: REQ-003 — Identity signals are normalized before comparison and storage
Source: intake WF-10 duplicate signals; DEC-002; DEC-003; Q5

The system MUST derive each identity signal with the normalization rules decided in Q5 and MUST store the normalized value, so that the database compares normalized values. If a signal is absent or normalizes to empty, then the system MUST treat it as not present: it MUST NOT match any other advertiser (DEC-003).

#### Scenario: Different spellings of the same domain normalize to one root domain
- GIVEN websites "https://www.acmeplumbing.com/contact" and "http://shop.acmeplumbing.com"
- WHEN their signals are derived
- THEN both have root domain "acmeplumbing.com"

#### Scenario: Missing phone never matches
- GIVEN advertisers A and B, both without a phone
- WHEN B is created
- THEN the absence of a phone does not count as a match between A and B

### Requirement: REQ-004 — Any matching signal is a duplicate
Source: intake WF-10 "matching ANY signal"

When an advertiser is created, or when an identity signal is added or changed, if any present signal equals the same signal of another advertiser, then the system MUST NOT create a second advertiser or assign that signal, and MUST respond as decided in Q2.

#### Scenario: Match on phone only
- GIVEN advertiser A has phone +14155550100
- WHEN a submission with a different Place ID, domain and name+ZIP but phone +14155550100 is made
- THEN no new advertiser is created and the response follows Q2

#### Scenario: Match on Place ID only
- GIVEN advertiser A has Place ID "ChIJ-acme"
- WHEN a submission with Place ID "ChIJ-acme" and all other signals different is made
- THEN no new advertiser is created and the response follows Q2

#### Scenario: Submission matches two different advertisers
- GIVEN advertiser A matches the submission on domain and advertiser B matches it on phone
- WHEN the submission is made
- THEN no new advertiser is created, and the response names both A and B (Q2)

#### Scenario: Editing an existing advertiser into a collision
- GIVEN advertiser A has phone +14155550100 and advertiser B has another phone
- WHEN B's phone is changed to +14155550100, or B gets a website on A's root domain
- THEN the change is rejected and B keeps its previous values

### Requirement: REQ-005 — At most one advertiser under concurrency, enforced by the database
Source: intake WF-10 concurrency AC; DEC-002; Q1

The database MUST reject any write that would give two advertisers the same present value of the same identity signal, for every writer listed under Invariants and Mechanism Proof. Concurrent submissions that match on any signal MUST therefore yield at most one advertiser, regardless of application-level checks.

#### Scenario: Two concurrent submissions share a root domain
- GIVEN no advertiser exists for acmeplumbing.com
- WHEN two submissions with root domain acmeplumbing.com but different names, phones and Place IDs commit concurrently
- THEN exactly one advertiser exists afterwards, and the other submission gets the Q2 response with no partial advertiser, website or signal rows

#### Scenario: Two concurrent submissions share different signals pairwise
- GIVEN submission S1 shares a phone with S2, and S2 shares a Place ID with S3
- WHEN S1, S2 and S3 commit concurrently
- THEN S2 never coexists with S1 or S3, and no two surviving advertisers share any signal

#### Scenario: Constraint holds without the application check
- GIVEN the application-level duplicate check is bypassed
- WHEN a row with a duplicate normalized signal is inserted directly
- THEN the database rejects the insert

### Requirement: REQ-006 — Existing data conforms before the constraint applies
Source: DEC-002; spec-quality-gates §1 (migration); Q3

When the uniqueness constraints are introduced, the system MUST handle existing advertisers that share a normalized signal as decided in Q3. It MUST NOT silently delete or merge advertiser data.

#### Scenario: Pre-existing duplicate pair
- GIVEN two existing advertisers that share root domain acmeplumbing.com
- WHEN the migration runs
- THEN the outcome follows Q3, and both advertisers' data remains recoverable

### Requirement: REQ-007 — Enrichment always reaches a terminal state
Source: intake WF-10 "retry or enter a visible failure state, never remain pending forever"; Q6

When enrichment of an advertiser from Google Places fails, the system MUST retry within the bound decided in Q6. If the bound is exhausted, or an attempt stops making progress (for example its worker dies), then the system MUST move the advertiser's enrichment to a failed state. No advertiser MAY stay in the pending enrichment state longer than the Q6 deadline.

#### Scenario: Transient failure then success
- GIVEN the first enrichment attempt times out
- WHEN a retry within the bound succeeds
- THEN the enrichment state is succeeded and the details are stored

#### Scenario: Retries exhausted
- GIVEN every attempt fails
- WHEN the retry bound is reached
- THEN the enrichment state is failed with the last error reason recorded

#### Scenario: Worker dies mid-attempt
- GIVEN an attempt was claimed and its worker stopped without finishing
- WHEN the Q6 progress deadline passes
- THEN the attempt is retried or marked failed; it is never left pending

### Requirement: REQ-008 — Enrichment failures and conflicts are visible
Source: intake WF-10 "visible failure state"; Q6; Q7

While an advertiser's enrichment is failed or in conflict, the system MUST show that state and its reason to the users decided in Q6, and MUST log it. When enrichment returns an identity signal (Place ID, phone, domain) that another advertiser already holds, the system MUST NOT assign it, and MUST handle the conflict as decided in Q7.

#### Scenario: Failed enrichment is shown
- GIVEN advertiser A's enrichment is failed
- WHEN an authorized user views A
- THEN they see the failed state and its reason

#### Scenario: Enrichment returns another advertiser's phone
- GIVEN advertiser B holds phone +14155550100
- WHEN A's enrichment returns phone +14155550100
- THEN A is not given that phone, and the outcome follows Q7

### Requirement: REQ-009 — Existing authorization is preserved
Source: spec-quality-gates §1 (authorization); Change Impact

The system MUST allow search and advertiser creation through this flow only to users who may create advertisers today.

#### Scenario: Unauthorized user
- GIVEN a user who cannot create advertisers today
- WHEN they call search or create
- THEN the request is refused and no Places call is made

## Material Decisions

### DEC-001 — Call Google Places directly, without the companion service
- Decision: this application calls the Google Places API itself for search and enrichment.
- Alternatives: reuse the companion service (single-place lookup only) or extend it.
- Reason: REQ-001 needs multi-result search; owner decision.
- Source: user decision in the /spec request, 2026-11-24
- Decided by: owner, 2026-11-24, /spec WF-10 request
- Affects: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-007

### DEC-002 — Database-enforced uniqueness for every identity signal
- Decision: the database enforces uniqueness for Place ID, normalized root domain, normalized name+ZIP and normalized phone.
- Alternatives: application-level checks (they race, per intake recon); enforcing only some signals.
- Reason: REQ-005; owner decision.
- Source: user decision in the /spec request, 2026-11-24
- Decided by: owner, 2026-11-24, /spec WF-10 request
- Affects: REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006

### DEC-003 — An absent signal never matches
- Decision: a signal that is missing or normalizes to empty does not participate in matching or uniqueness.
- Alternatives: treat an empty value as a value, so that two advertisers without a phone would collide.
- Reason: a match needs a value to compare; the ticket defines duplicates by matching signals (intake WF-10).
- Source: intake WF-10 duplicate-signal definition
- Decided by: default (interactive)
- Affects: REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005

### DEC-004 — 10 s timeout per Google Places request
- Decision: each Places request times out after 10 s. In enrichment, a timeout counts as one failed attempt.
- Alternatives: no explicit timeout (the platform default, which may hang).
- Reason: REQ-002 and REQ-007 need a measurable failure trigger. Low risk, recommended option.
- Source: spec-quality-gates §1 (timeout)
- Decided by: default (interactive)
- Affects: REQ-002, REQ-007

## Tech Stack
Not surveyed: the fixture holds no WF-10 application code, and further recon was unavailable in this trial. External dependency: Google Places API (DEC-001); the exact endpoints are chosen in /plan.

## Commands
- Verification: `python3 verify.py` (from `AGENTS.md`; found in source, not executed in this run).
- Other build/test/lint commands: unresolved; no repository-defined command was found.

## Project Structure
Specs live in `requirements/`, plans and tasks in `work/` (`AGENTS.md`). The modules for advertisers, websites, search and enrichment are Not surveyed.

## Code Style
Not surveyed.

## Testing Strategy
- REQ-001/002: integration tests with a stubbed Places client covering multiple results, zero results, timeout, quota error and key redaction. No live Google calls in tests.
- REQ-003: unit tests over the normalization table decided in Q5.
- REQ-004: integration tests, one per signal, the two-advertiser match, and update paths (name/ZIP/phone edits, website add/change).
- REQ-005: database-level constraint tests, one per signal, that bypass the application. Concurrency tests run parallel transactions on a real database, starting from an empty store and from existing related rows, and assert that the resulting count is 1 or less.
- REQ-006: a migration test on a seeded duplicate pair.
- REQ-007/008: job tests with retries exhausted, a stale claim past the deadline, success after retry, and an enrichment conflict.
- REQ-009: authorization tests for search and create.
- Every test maps to its REQ id. Runner: `python3 verify.py`; other runners unresolved.

## Invariants and Mechanism Proof
- Invariant: for each signal type s in {place_id, root_domain, name_zip, phone} and each present normalized value v, at most one advertiser holds (s, v). Absent signals hold nothing (DEC-003). Empty state: no advertisers means no holders.
- Writers that can establish or transfer a signal: advertiser create; edits to name, ZIP or phone; website add/change/remove, since root domain lives on the separate website table; enrichment writing a Place ID, phone or domain; and the migration/backfill. Release: advertiser deletion or archival (Q4), and website removal. All writers in the code are **Not surveyed**. /plan MUST run a change-surface search for every one of them.
- Serialization point: unresolved, pending **Q1**. A transaction alone does not serialize these writes. A per-column unique index on the website table does not on its own say how one advertiser with several websites on the same root domain is handled.
- No child row yet: the claim must be taken in the same transaction that creates the advertiser, so the first creator wins even when no website or advertiser row exists yet.
- Guarantees: the database guarantees at most one holder. The application guarantees normalization (REQ-003), the Q2 response, and rollback of partial rows.
- Evidence: constraint tests per signal and concurrency tests (Testing Strategy).

## Data Lifecycle
Whether advertisers or websites have soft-delete or archive fields is **Not surveyed**. Q4 decides whether deleted or archived advertisers keep their signals, which governs uniqueness, restoration and reads. Website removal releases that website's root domain only if no other website of the same advertiser has it.

## Boundaries
- Always: normalize before storing; enforce uniqueness in the database; keep the API key server-side.
- Ask first: deleting or merging existing advertisers; changing the companion service.
- Never: rely on application-only duplicate checks for the guarantee; leave enrichment pending without a deadline.

## Open Questions

OPEN QUESTION: Q1 — Constraint shape that covers every writer, including root domain on the website table
- Option A (recommended — one unique constraint covers all four signals and every writer, including the separate website table, and a single table can be added and dropped without touching existing rows): an identity-claim table with a unique key on (signal_type, normalized_value) and an advertiser reference. Every writer inserts or deletes its claims in the same transaction as its own row change.
- Option B: per-signal unique indexes on the owning tables: Place ID, phone and (name, ZIP) on the advertiser table, root domain on the website table. Simpler, but one advertiser cannot have two websites on the same root domain, and website writers must run in the advertiser's transaction.
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q2 — Response to a duplicate or losing concurrent submission
- Option A (recommended — never attaches one submitter's data to an existing advertiser, and keeps existing data unchanged): reject with a duplicate error naming every matched advertiser and the matched signals.
- Option B: if exactly one advertiser matches, return it as the result without changing it; if several match, reject as in A.
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q3 — Existing rows that already violate the new uniqueness
- Option A (recommended — keeps all data, and the migration can be undone): the migration first reports every conflicting group and stops. The owner resolves the conflicts, then the constraint is applied.
- Option B: merge each conflicting group into its oldest advertiser automatically, keeping an audit record.
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q4 — Do deleted or archived advertisers keep their identity signals?
- Option A (recommended — keeps data, and restoring an advertiser never collides): yes. A deleted or archived advertiser still holds its signals, and new matching submissions are rejected and point at it.
- Option B: deletion or archival releases the signals, so a new advertiser may take them. Restoring then fails if the signals were taken meanwhile.
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q5 — Normalization rules
- Option A (recommended — uses standard, reversible-to-explain rules and the narrowest matching that still catches formatting variants): root domain is the registrable domain from the Public Suffix List, lowercased, with scheme, subdomains, port and path stripped. Phone is E.164, defaulting to region US. Name is Unicode case-folded and trimmed, with whitespace collapsed and punctuation removed; legal suffixes (Inc, LLC) are kept. ZIP is the first 5 digits.
- Option B: as A, but name normalization also strips legal suffixes, so "Acme Plumbing LLC" matches "Acme Plumbing".
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q6 — Retry bound, stuck-attempt deadline and failure visibility
- Option A (recommended — meets "retry or visible failure" fully, with a measurable deadline): up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff, all within 1 hour. An attempt with no progress after 10 minutes counts as failed. The final state is failed, shown on the advertiser to every user who can view it, with a manual retry action.
- Option B: no automatic retry. The first failure sets the failed state immediately, with a manual retry action.
- Risk: Medium
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.

OPEN QUESTION: Q7 — Enrichment returns a signal another advertiser holds
- Option A (recommended — keeps both advertisers' data unchanged and visible for review): store the non-conflicting details and set the enrichment state to conflict, naming the other advertiser and the signal.
- Option B: discard the whole enrichment result and mark the enrichment failed.
- Risk: High
→ Decision needed before this spec can be approved.
